html:
SMTO-CTX-0034 — This step has no saved result yet

GUID: 9e29bb95-ce06-519f-944f-a46bb6d4e6b8
Slug: result-pending
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: stored-result-recovery

What happened

  • The task asked for the result of one of its steps, but that step has no saved result yet. It may still be running, or it may have stopped without saving one. Nothing new was started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the task's activity to see whether that step is still running. A step that is still running saves its result only when it finishes.
  2. Give the step time to finish; the task is told to check the step's status instead of guessing. Once the result is saved, the task can read it normally.
  3. If the step seems stuck, check its target (for example the file or system it was changing) before asking for it again. The step may have already made its change even though no result was saved.

What success looks like

  • The step shows as finished and the task reads its result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask the task to start the same step again until you have confirmed it didn't already make its change.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The receipt resolver found an accessible recorded operation whose record does not yet name a captured receipt, so read_result returned incomplete with a task_context.read action for the operation.

What this means

  • The resolver found an operation in the authorized source scope, but its record does not name a captured receipt. It returns an incomplete result and a task_context.read action for that operation. The record may still be pending; this condition alone does not prove that a process is running.

Why this can happen

  • The resolver found an operation in the authorized source scope, but its record does not name a captured receipt. It returns an incomplete result and a task_context.read action for that operation. The record may still be pending; this condition alone does not prove that a process is running.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the operation record rather than guessing a receipt ID or starting another operation.

How to fix it

  • Read the operation's recorded state through the returned task_context.read next_action and follow its existing wait or continuation; read the receipt only once the record names one. A missing receipt does not prove the operation is running, stopped or never started, so do not relaunch it.
  • Read the operation's recorded state using next_action and follow its existing wait or continuation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Read the existing operation state; try its receipt only after the record advertises one.

How to verify the fix

  • The existing operation eventually advertises a readable receipt or records its terminal outcome.

What not to do

  • Do not relaunch the operation or infer that the missing receipt proves no external work occurred.

Technical notes

  • The lookup is incomplete and launches no work; prior external effects are not established.
  • A missing captured receipt does not prove that execution is running, stopped or never started.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
